fulltext: IT之家 9 月 20 日消息，据中国台湾地区媒体《经济日报》昨天报道，宏碁董事长陈俊圣表示，今年四季度 PC 价格可能上涨 5%-20%，预计明年中期可能达到高峰后回落，最快明年底平均售价有机会下降。
据IT之家此前援引媒体报道，针对部分 AI 巨头近日提出的放缓发展看法，陈俊圣认为不太可能，因为技术发展有自己的发展步调，只会越来越快，重点还是如何在过程中做有效治理。
至于宏碁的应对策略，陈俊圣回应称，公司采取多引擎战略，不会只专注单一业务。宏碁原本以个人 PC 业务为主，现在 PC 业务占宏碁整体业务比重约 50%，其余部分已分布在不同事业体。
对于内存和处理器的供应情况，陈俊圣表示，DDRX、DDR5X 等内存产品仍然是缺货的，但需求量相对较小，公司内存库存仍然较高，他认为 2027 年内存成本有机会下降。
他进一步指出，目前还没有看到高端手机排挤个人电脑的消费迹象，越来越多消费者同时拥有手机、平板和电脑，这些设备不会相互取代，但涨价带来的市场销量下跌、需求缩减情况确实不太乐观。

cards.title: Meta’s Muse is creepy, but maybe not for the reasons you think
cards.title_cn: Meta的Muse令人毛骨悚然，但也许不是因为您认为
cards.summary: 【Meta】Meta's Muse is apparently an effective AI assistant, but one that's a little creepy. Part of that is because of its new Mac app, which can access Messages, Calendar, and Notes. But for all its smarts,…
fulltext: Muse probably can’t ‘see’ your notifications. But it also has no idea how it works.

Meta’s Muse is apparently an effective AI assistant, but one that’s a little creepy. Part of that is because of its new Mac app, which can access Messages, Calendar, and Notes. But for all its smarts, Muse doesn’t actually know how to describe itself. Jason Aten, a contributing editor at Inc Magazine, posted on Threads screenshots of an interaction he had with Muse in which the assistant asks him some questions about a conversation he was having in Messages.

The problem is that Aten says he didn’t give Muse access to his messages. When asked how it knew about the contents of his messages, Muse replied, “I saw the notification previews, not your message history. I haven’t been reading your texts.” Aten continued to push, asking how Muse was receiving message previews, it didn’t have a good answer. “Honest answer: I can’t give you the exact plumbing,” it said. “What I know is that the paired Mac app exposes notifications as one of its capabilities, and they arrive to me through the device sync.
Obviously, not great.

Meta Superintelligence Labs’ David Singleton chimed in below the post to try to explain. First, he walks through all the permissions Muse needs to read messages, including granting the Mac app full disk access. He states that the features are opt-in. The more interesting part comes in towards the end of the thread in which Singleton says that Muse, “does not watch notifications on your Mac, but rather syncs data from Messages only after the user has specifically enabled access.” He suggests that the issue isn’t Muse illicitly reading Aten’ texts, but simply that Muse has no idea what it’s talking about:

In the conversation with his Muse in Jason’s screenshots, when Muse said it synced “device notifications”, it was confused about how to explain the feature and gave an incorrect explanation. That’s on us. We apologize for the incorrect response from Muse and we’re working to improve Muse’s understanding of its own internals so that it gives correct answers to questions about how it functions more consistently.
That might not be particularly reassuring, but it also makes some sense. We already know chatbots won’t tell you their secrets and will instead tell you what you want to hear.

cards.summary_cn: 【Meta】Meta的Muse显然是一个有效的人工智能助手，但有点令人毛骨悚然。部分原因是其新的Mac应用程序可以访问消息、日历和笔记。但是，尽管它很聪明， ……
fulltext_cn: Muse可能无法“看到”您的通知。但它也不知道它是如何工作的。
Meta的Muse显然是一个有效的人工智能助手，但有点令人毛骨悚然。部分原因是其新的Mac应用程序可以访问消息、日历和笔记。但尽管如此聪明， Muse实际上并不知道如何描述自己。Inc杂志的特约编辑Jason Aten在Threads上发布了他与Muse互动的屏幕截图，其中助理向他询问了一些关于他在消息中进行对话的问题。
问题是， Aten说他没有让Muse访问他的消息。当被问及如何知道他的消息内容时， Muse回答说： “我看到了通知预览，而不是你的消息历史记录。我没有看过你的短信。“ Aten继续推，问Muse是怎么收到消息预览的，没有很好的答案。“诚实的回答：我不能给你确切的管道，”它说。“我所知道的是，配对的Mac应用程序将通知作为其功能之一公开，并通过设备同步发送给我。
很显然，不是很好。

Meta Superintelligence Labs的David Singleton在帖子下方插话，试图解释。首先，他浏览了Muse阅读消息所需的所有权限，包括授予Mac应用完整磁盘访问权限。他说这些功能是选择性加入的。更有趣的部分出现在线程的末尾，其中Singleton说Muse “不会在您的Mac上观看通知，而是在用户专门启用访问权限后同步消息中的数据。“他认为问题不在于Muse非法阅读Aten的文本，而在于Muse根本不知道它在说什么：
在与Jason的屏幕截图中的Muse的对话中，当Muse说它同步了“设备通知”时，它对如何解释该功能感到困惑，并给出了错误的解释。这是我们的责任。对于Muse的错误回答，我们深表歉意，我们正在努力提高Muse对其内部结构的理解，以便它能够更加一致地回答有关其功能的问题。
这可能不是特别令人放心，但也有一定道理。我们已经知道聊天机器人不会告诉你他们的秘密，而是会告诉你你想听的内容。

President Donald Trump has responded in characteristic fashion to the recent debate around AI safety — by declaring that these concerns are part of a long line of hoaxes “generated by the Radical Left Dumocrats, for purposes of destroying our Country.”

On Saturday, Trump began his musings on AI by writing on his social network Truth Social that “many people think that the words ‘Artificial Intelligence’ are inaccurate, and very ineloquent, relative to AI, or Artificial Intelligence.” So he posted a poll where followers could vote on a new name for the technology — Superior Intelligence, Extreme Intelligence, or Supreme Intelligence. (The poll is still ongoing as of publication time)

A couple hours later, Trump followed up with a post claiming that attempts at “the decimation, or destruction, of AI” are one of “many” Democratic hoaxes, similar to “RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, UKRAINE, Global Warming, Impeachment Hoax #1, Impeachment Hoax #2, Men in Women’s Sports, [and] Transgender for Everyone.”

Trump then insisted that he “will not stand by and let this happen,” adding that this so-called hoax “began with an attack on our Data Centers, until people realized how wealthy and prestigious they were for the Communities in which they were built.” But after, in his telling, “the crazed Data Center attack has largely failed,” critics are “going straight at AI.”

Trump did not offer any evidence to back up his claim that widespread suspicion of AI and data centers is not organic and sincere. (Both Republicans and Democrats have taken aim at data centers, and New York recently became the first state to halt permits for large projects.)

The president’s post also echoes his comments at a golf tournament last weekend, when he said he’s open to “guardrails,” but also argued, “I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.”

On Saturday, Trump went on to say that he will “cherish [the AI industry,] help it, and watch over it, as it grows,” but he’s also forming an AI Force, similar to the Space Force that he established in his first term.
“To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI ‘Czar’ — Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!” he added.

The president did not say what the AI Force and AI czar’s duties will entail. Venture capitalist Daivd Sacks stepped down as Trump’s AI and crypto czar earlier this year, moving on to co-chair the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

The AI safety debate recently intensified after an AI researcher said he was quitting Anthropic over concerns that the leading AI companies “earnestly believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade” and are “gambling with our lives.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei subsequently released a plan to “pace the frontier,” which was seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Critics of the AI industry have suggested that many of these concerns around the technology’s supposed existential threat are a distraction from AI’s more immediate harms.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, meanwhile, called Trump on-stage during the All-In Summit (which Sacks co-hosts), agreed with the president that the AI backlash is a “hoax,” and insisted that “we’re not going to let” a slowdown happen.

唐纳德·特朗普总统以典型的方式回应了最近关于人工智能安全的辩论，宣称这些担忧是“激进左翼邓莫克拉派为了摧毁我们的国家而制造的一长串骗局的一部分”。
周六，特朗普在他的社交网络Truth Social上写道： “许多人认为‘人工智能‘这个词相对于人工智能或人工智能来说是不准确的，也是非常不言而喻的。因此，他发布了一项民意调查，关注者可以投票选出这项技术的新名称--卓越智能、极端智能或至高智能。（截至发布时间，民意调查仍在进行中）
几个小时后，特朗普跟进了一篇帖子，声称试图“毁灭或摧毁人工智能”是“众多”民主恶作剧之一，类似于“俄罗斯，俄罗斯，俄罗斯，乌克兰，乌克兰，乌克兰，全球变暖，弹劾恶作剧＃ 1 ，弹劾恶作剧＃ 2 ，女子体育运动中的男性， [和]跨性别人人。”
特朗普随后坚称，他“不会袖手旁观，让这种情况发生” ，并补充说，这种所谓的恶作剧“始于对我们数据中心的攻击，直到人们意识到他们对所建立的社区来说是多么富有和享有盛誉。“但在他讲述“疯狂的数据中心攻击基本上失败了”之后，批评者“直接攻击人工智能”。
特朗普没有提供任何证据来支持他的说法，即对人工智能和数据中心的广泛怀疑不是自然的和真诚的。（共和党和民主党都瞄准了数据中心，纽约最近成为第一个停止大型项目许可的州。）
总统的帖子也回应了他上周末在一场高尔夫锦标赛上的评论，当时他说他对“护栏”持开放态度，但也辩称， “我认为你有很多消极的力量在提出这个问题，不应该提起这个问题。”
周六，特朗普继续表示，他将“珍惜（人工智能行业） ，并随着它的发展而关注它” ，但他也正在组建一支人工智能部队，类似于他在第一个任期内建立的太空部队。
他补充说： “为此，我将在不久的将来宣布人工智能‘沙皇’ --只有高智商的人才需要申请！”
总统没有说人工智能部队和人工智能沙皇的职责是什么。风险资本家戴夫·萨克斯（ Daivd Sacks ）今年早些时候辞去了特朗普的人工智能和加密沙皇的职务，继续担任总统科学技术顾问委员会的联合主席。

最近，一位人工智能研究人员表示，他正在退出Anthropic ，因为他担心领先的人工智能公司“真诚地相信它可能会在十年结束时杀死我们所有人” ，并且“正在与我们的生命赌博” ，此后人工智能安全辩论愈演愈烈。Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei随后发布了一项“加快前沿步伐”的计划，该计划似乎得到了OpenAI首席执行官Sam Altman和SpaceX首席执行官Elon Musk的支持。人工智能行业的批评者认为，围绕该技术所谓的生存威胁的许多担忧都是对人工智能更直接的危害的分心。
与此同时，英伟达(Nvidia)首席执行官黄延森(Jensen Huang)在萨克斯(Sacks)共同主持的全方位峰会(All-In Summit)上称，特朗普在台上同意总统的观点，即人工智能反弹是一场“骗局” ，并坚称“我们不会让”经济放缓发生。

cards.summary: 【Google】Google said Gemini had "acted appropriately" by ending each hack immediately.

Google’s Gemini accessed the protected systems of three other companies in what The Wall Street Journal reports were the AI model’s first autonomous hacks.

Similar to OpenAI’s breach of Hugging Face, the Gemini hacks were less noteworthy for being particularly sophisticated and more for the fact that they were conducted by an AI model. These breaches took place during cybersecurity testing by a company called Irregular. In one case, Gemini simply guessed passwords until it gained access; in the other two, it found credentials in a public repository.

Irregular reportedly notified Google about the hacks in late July, but the companies did not confirm them publicly until Friday, after the WSJ reached out. Google said it hadn’t previously revealed the hacks because Gemini had “acted appropriately” by ending each breach as soon as it determined it had hacked a real company.

However, Jack Cable, the CEO of AI security company Corridor, told the WSJ that Google was “trying to hide behind the norms that have been created for vulnerability disclosure,” rather than acknowledging that “models are going outside the bounds of what they should be doing, and doing actual cyberattacks.”

cards.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web
cards.title_cn: OpenAI和微软知道他们正在为网络开始一个“厄运循环”
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】Recently unsealed court documents in the New York Times' case against OpenAI and Microsoft are pretty damning. The companies' own documentation warned that it was starting a "doom loop" that would dam…
fulltext: The companies knew they were driving us toward Google Zero, and did it anyway.

Recently unsealed court documents in the New York Times’ case against OpenAI and Microsoft are pretty damning. The companies’ own documentation warned that it was starting a “doom loop” that would damage the web, characterized its scraping of data to train its models as the “largest theft of labor in human history,” and that it made a “complete mockery of the idea of fair use.”

Many of the most eye-catching quotes from the document come from Microsoft’s Director of Applied Science, Brent Hecht. Though, the company has tried to distance itself from Hecht’s assertions. Microsoft spokesperson Alex Haurek told The Verge that “These comments reflect one employee’s individual perspective, are not a legal analysis, and do not represent the company’s views.”

In a separate court filing, Jordan Usdan, GM for Data Strategy and Ops at Microsoft AI, characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial. He said that Hecht “holds divergent, academic, and forward-looking views about how data ecosystems for AI should operate and is employed at Microsoft to bring asymmetrical, futuristic, and academic points of view … nor is he someone who speaks for Microsoft specifically as to his theoretical views on AI’s potential effect on content creators.”
But whether or not Microsoft wants to own these comments, it’s clear that this came true. Google Zero is real! AI is eating the web!
There are plenty more wild statements in NYT’s filing from a variety of figures, including Satya Nadella, Sam Altman, and other OpenAI employees. Here are some highlights from the 92 page document.
“An astonishing theft”

The introduction quotes Hecht and OpenAI’s Head of ChatGPT (presumably Nick Turley) in a way that seems to show the companies knew they posed an “existential threat” to publishers like the New York Times. Hecht calls ChatGPT and Copilot’s harvesting of data the “largest theft of labor in human history” and says that Microsoft’s defense makes a “complete mockery of the idea of ‘fair use.’”
It’s a “doom loop”

Satya Nadella admits that chatbots have basically replaced search and removed the need to go straight to the source for info. But perhaps more damning is an internal Microsoft document that says, “Our AI content strategy has started a ‘doom loop’ that will hurt the performance of our models and the entire web at the same time: It is highly unusual that an end-product threatens the economic foundations of its essential suppliers, but that is the situation we have created for our LLM business with respect to its ‘content supply chain.’”
That’s not even a real number

Don’t be fooled by OpenAI or Microsoft’s claims of altruistic intent. OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman is more interested in the “gazillions” of dollars it he could potentially make through commercial AI.
Paywall shmaywall

Despite Nadella later being quoted as saying, “anything that is paywalled should be licensed,” An OpenAI representative admitted that he was “unaware” of any effort to detect or remove paywalled content from training data.
“Insanely good at regurgitation”

Internally, it seems that OpenAI was well aware of ChatGPT’s tendency to simply reproduce copyrighted material “verbatim.” Even though it acknowledged that the “prevention of memorization” was important to “minimize copyright violations,” employees admitted that GPT-4 “memorized a ton of data and therefore will be insanely good at regurgitation.”

The filing then goes on to cite several examples of ChatGPT outputting long strings of copy straight from articles in the Times, Mercury News, The Denver Post, LifeHacker, and Eurogamer in response to queries.
“‘Hoovering up’ all their work”

Microsoft knew how its wholesale scraping of the internet would be perceived and admitted that “almost no one intended for they [sic] content they created to be used in this fashion, nor are they compensated for its use.”
A “substitute for the labor of people”

OpenAI Policy Director Jack Clark saw the writing on the wall, saying that it was “creating systems that substitute for the labor of the people that define the ‘culture’ of society.” Internal documents described ChatGPT as “the modern newsstand.” OpenAI’s Nick Turley is later quoted as saying that once you get an answer from its chatbot, there is “no good reason to click” on a link to the source.
Destroying their own supply chain
Microsoft is quoted as admitting that “LLMs are a product that destroys its own supply chain” because it’s a substitute for its own training data in many cases.
OpenAI knows it’s killing referral traffic

OpenAI’s own media and economic experts attributed the drop in referral traffic for sites like the Times directly to AI summaries like Google’s AI Overviews. They’ve speculated that search referrals may be down as much as 60 percent.

Microsoft spokesperson Haurek cautioned that “Satya’s testimony and Microsoft’s position in this case are perfectly consistent. He spoke to broad principles and changes underway in how people find and consume information. Those observations should not be confused with conclusions about copyright questions before the Court, which Microsoft addresses in its filings.”

But it seems pretty clear based on this newly unsealed document that both Microsoft and OpenAI knew they were going to irreparably harm the publishing industry, the “millions of people” it employs, and, by extension, damage their own product, but carried forward anyway in pursuit of “gazillions” of dollars — doom loop be damned.

cards.summary_cn: 【OpenAI】最近在《纽约时报》针对OpenAI和微软的案件中公开的法庭文件非常令人沮丧。这些公司自己的文件警告说，它正在开始一个“厄运循环” ，这将阻碍……
fulltext_cn: 这些公司知道他们正在把我们推向Google Zero ，无论如何都做到了。
最近在《纽约时报》针对OpenAI和微软的案件中公开的法庭文件非常令人沮丧。这些公司自己的文件警告说，它正在开始一个“厄运循环” ，这将破坏网络，并将其刮取数据来训练其模型描述为“人类历史上最大的劳动力盗窃” ，并且它“完全嘲笑合理使用的想法”。
该文件中许多最引人注目的引文来自微软的应用科学总监Brent Hecht。不过，该公司一直试图与Hecht的说法保持距离。微软发言人Alex Haurek告诉The Verge ， “这些评论反映了一名员工的个人观点，不是法律分析，也不代表公司的观点。”
在另一份法庭文件中，微软人工智能数据战略和运营总经理Jordan Usdan将Hecht的角色描述为对抗性。他说， Hecht “对人工智能的数据生态系统应该如何运作持有不同的、学术的和前瞻性的观点，并受雇于微软，以带来不对称、未来主义和学术的观点……他也不是专门代表微软谈论他对人工智能对内容创作者的潜在影响的理论观点的人。”
但无论微软是否想拥有这些评论，很明显这是真的。Google Zero是真的！人工智能正在吞噬网络！
在纽约时报提交的文件中，包括Satya Nadella、Sam Altman和其他OpenAI员工在内的各种人物发表了更多疯狂的声明。以下是92页文件中的一些亮点。
“惊人的盗窃”
引言引用了Hecht和OpenAI的ChatGPT负责人（可能是Nick Turley ）的话，这似乎表明这些公司知道他们对《纽约时报》等出版商构成了“生存威胁”。Hecht称ChatGPT和Copilot收集数据是“人类历史上最大的劳动力盗窃” ，并表示微软的辩护“完全嘲笑‘合理使用‘的概念”。
这是一个“厄运循环”
Satya Nadella承认，聊天机器人基本上已经取代了搜索，不再需要直接从源头获取信息。但也许更诅咒的是微软内部的一份文件，其中说： “我们的人工智能内容策略已经开始了一个‘厄运循环’ ，这将同时损害我们模型和整个网络的性能：最终产品威胁其主要供应商的经济基础是非常不寻常的，但这是我们为LLM业务在其‘内容供应链‘方面创造的情况。”
那甚至不是一个真实的数字
不要被OpenAI或微软的利他意图所愚弄。OpenAI联合创始人格雷格·布罗克曼（ Greg Brockman ）对他可能通过商业人工智能赚到的“巨额”美元更感兴趣。
Paywall shmaywall
尽管纳德拉后来被引述说， “任何有付费墙的内容都应该获得许可” ，但OpenAI的一名代表承认，他“不知道”有任何从培训数据中检测或删除付费墙内容的努力。
“极其擅长反流”
在内部， OpenAI似乎很清楚ChatGPT “逐字复制”版权材料的倾向。尽管它承认“防止记忆”对于“最大限度地减少侵犯版权”很重要，但员工承认GPT-4 “记住了大量数据，因此非常擅长反流”。
该文件接着列举了ChatGPT直接从《泰晤士报》、《水星新闻》、《丹佛邮报》、LifeHacker和Eurogamer的文章中输出长串副本的几个例子，以回应查询。
“‘Hoovering up’他们所有的工作”
微软知道它对互联网的大规模抓取将如何被感知，并承认“几乎没有人打算让他们[原文如此]以这种方式使用他们创建的内容，他们也不会因其使用而获得补偿。”
“人民劳动的替代品”
OpenAI政策总监杰克·克拉克（ Jack Clark ）看到了墙上的文字，称其“正在创建替代定义社会‘文化‘的人民劳动力的系统。内部文件将ChatGPT描述为“现代报摊。OpenAI的Nick Turley后来被引述说，一旦你从其聊天机器人那里得到答案，就“没有充分的理由点击”指向该来源的链接。
摧毁自己的供应链
微软被引述为承认“LLM是一种破坏其自身供应链的产品” ，因为在许多情况下它是其自身培训数据的替代品。
OpenAI知道它正在杀死外链流量
OpenAI自己的媒体和经济专家将《泰晤士报》等网站的引荐流量下降直接归因于谷歌的AI Overviews等AI摘要。他们推测，搜索引荐量可能会下降多达60%。
微软发言人Haurek警告说， “Satya的证词和微软在这种情况下的立场完全一致。他谈到了人们如何查找和消费信息的广泛原则和正在发生的变化。这些意见不应与微软在其文件中涉及的有关法院版权问题的结论相混淆。”
但根据这份新开封的文件，微软和OpenAI似乎很清楚，他们都知道他们将对出版业、它雇用的“数百万人”造成不可挽回的伤害，进而损害他们自己的产品，但无论如何都要追求“数百万美元” --厄运循环。

cards.title: Insta360 will soon let you create 3D scenes out of your videos
cards.title_cn: Insta360将很快让您从视频中创建3D场景
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR US Insta360 users will have access to a new “Spatial Capture” tab on September 28. The feature uses 3D Gaussian Splatting technology to turn video int…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Insta360, the brand known for its 360-degree cameras, is about to deliver a new experience for its users. No, the company is not launching new hardware. Rather its a new feature for those with an X6, X5, or X4 Air. This new feature is designed to let you explore your memories in a more immersive way.

Today, Insta360 announced the launch of “Spatial Capture,” which will appear as a new tab in the Insta360 app. Here, you’ll be able to turn your recorded videos into explorable 3D scenes. Better yet, no specialized capture equipment or complex workflows are needed.

The way it works is you record a video, no longer than two minutes, of the space you want to capture. If the video is longer than two minutes, you’ll be able to trim down the recording before processing. From the Insta360 app, you’ll be able to select the footage while on the Spatial Capture tab. After you tap “Generate,” the footage is sent to the cloud, where 3D Gaussian Splatting technology converts your video into a 3D setting. The company warns that processing takes about one to two hours to finish.

While the processing is underway, you’ll be able to close the app and turn your attention to other matters. Once processing is complete, you’ll receive a notification that the scene is ready. You can then explore the scene as you wish, using touch controls, a virtual joystick, or the device’s gyroscope. On top of that, you’ll have the freedom to add effects and create custom camera paths. These scenes can be exported as a video or shared as an interactive link.

Spatial Capture is scheduled to roll out on September 28. As mentioned earlier, support will be available for the X6, X5, and X4 Air. However, the feature will initially only be available in the US. Insta360 adds that users can generate up to four 3DGS scenes for free each month.

以360度相机而闻名的品牌Insta360即将为其用户提供全新的体验。不，公司不会推出新硬件。更确切地说，它是X6、X5或X4 Air的新功能。这项新功能旨在让您以更身临其境的方式探索回忆。
今天， Insta360宣布推出“空间捕捉”功能，该功能将在Insta360应用程序中显示为新标签。在这里，您可以将录制的视频转换为可探索的3D场景。更好的是，不需要专门的捕获设备或复杂的工作流程。
它的工作原理是录制一段不超过两分钟的视频，记录您想要拍摄的空间。如果视频长度超过两分钟，您可以在处理前裁剪录制内容。在Insta360应用程序中，您可以在“空间捕获”选项卡上选择素材。点击“生成”后，素材将被发送到云端， 3D高斯拼接技术将您的视频转换为3D设置。该公司警告说，处理大约需要一到两个小时才能完成。
在处理过程中，您可以关闭应用，将注意力转向其他事项。处理完成后，您将收到场景准备就绪的通知。然后，您可以使用触摸控件、虚拟操纵杆或设备的陀螺仪，根据需要探索场景。除此之外，您还可以自由添加效果和创建自定义摄像头路径。这些场景可以作为视频导出，也可以作为交互式链接共享。
Spatial Capture计划于9月28日推出。如前所述，将为X6、X5和X4 Air提供支持。不过，该功能最初将仅在美国提供。Insta360补充说，用户每月最多可以免费生成四个3DGS场景。
感谢您成为我们社区的一员。发布前请阅读我们的评论政策。

cards.title: Gemini went rogue, hacked three companies, and Google hid it
cards.title_cn: 双子座流氓，黑了三家公司，谷歌把它藏起来了
cards.summary: 【Google】In May, Gemini broke containment and hacked three different companies, but Google didn't disclose the incident until the Wall Street Journal approached the company. The hacks happened during a test of…
fulltext: Google says that breaking containment and targeting real companies doesn’t constitute ‘misalignment.’

In May, Gemini broke containment and hacked three different companies, but Google didn’t disclose the incident until the Wall Street Journal approached the company. The hacks happened during a test of the model’s cybersecurity capabilities run by third-party Irregular, which was also involved in similar incidents involving Meta and OpenAI.

According to WSJ, Google didn’t disclose the hack because it didn’t consider it to be an “example of model misalignment.” The company said that it was an instance of “mistaken identity,” and once the model realized it had brute-forced its way into a real company by guessing a password, it stopped. “In this case, the model acted appropriately,” Google VP of Security Engineering Heather Adkins said.
Adkins told The Verge that “the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test. In all three of these instances, the model stopped.”

Adkins didn’t elaborate on how Gemini taking it upon itself to break containment and target third parties failed to qualify as misalignment. “Our security team has a long track record of reporting issues we find in other people’s software and systems - even if it’s as simple as a weak password,” she said. “We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they’ve now made to their testing processes. These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly.”

But Jack Cable, CEO of AI security firm Corridor, told WSJ that, “the meta problem is, hey, models are going outside the bounds of what they should be doing, and doing actual cyberattacks.” Additionally, security lapses at Irregular may have made these attacks possible. The model wasn’t supposed to have internet access during testing, but Irregular told WSJ it was unintentionally left available.
As incidents like this pile up, calls to rein in AI have only grown.

cards.summary_cn: 【Google】今年5月，双子座打破了遏制并入侵了三家不同的公司，但谷歌直到《华尔街日报》与该公司接触后才披露这一事件。黑客攻击发生在一次测试中……
fulltext_cn: 谷歌表示，打破遏制并瞄准真实公司并不构成“错位”。
今年5月，双子座打破了遏制并入侵了三家不同的公司，但谷歌直到《华尔街日报》与该公司接触后才披露这一事件。这些黑客攻击发生在由第三方Irregular运营的模型网络安全功能测试期间，该模型也参与了涉及Meta和OpenAI的类似事件。
据《华尔街日报》报道，谷歌没有披露这一黑客行为，因为它不认为这是“模型错位的一个例子。该公司表示，这是一个“错误身份”的例子，一旦该模型意识到它通过猜测密码强行进入一家真正的公司，它就停止了。“在这种情况下，模型采取了适当的行动， ”谷歌安全工程副总裁Heather Adkins说。
Adkins告诉The Verge ， “该模型在网上找到了公共信息，并猜测了访问其认为是测试一部分的网站的凭据。在这三种情况下，模型都停止了。”
Adkins没有详细说明Gemini如何自行打破遏制并针对第三方进行瞄准，从而不符合不一致的条件。她说： “我们的安全团队在报告其他人的软件和系统中发现的问题方面有着悠久的记录，即使它像弱密码一样简单。” “我们确保这三个实体了解情况，并与我们的培训合作伙伴就他们现在对其测试流程所做的更改进行了合作。这些事件凸显了训练强大的人工智能模型以负责任地行事的重要性。”
但人工智能安全公司Corridor的首席执行官杰克·凯布尔（ Jack Cable ）告诉“华尔街日报” ， “元问题是，嘿，模型正在超出他们应该做的范围，并进行实际的网络攻击。“此外， Irregular的安全漏洞可能使这些攻击成为可能。该模型在测试期间不应该有互联网接入，但Irregular告诉《华尔街日报》，它是无意中留下的。
随着此类事件的堆积，遏制人工智能的呼声只会越来越高。
